title: Formal local equation at a split node
statement: Let $f:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $t\in T$ map to $s\in S$, and assume that $f$ is flat at $t$ [def-weil-flat-morphism], $\mathcal O_{S,s}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $f$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Suppose $t$ is a split node of the fibre $T_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]: $t$ is closed in that fibre [def-weil-closed-points], $\kappa(t)=\kappa(s)$ through the induced residue-field map [def-weil-residue-field], and $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T_s,t}\cong\kappa(s)[[u,v]]/(uv)$ as $\kappa(s)$-algebras. Then there exist $h\in\mathfrak m_s\widehat{\mathcal O}_{S,s}$ and an isomorphism of $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{S,s}$-algebras $$\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T,t}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{S,s}[[u,v]]/(uv-h).$$ All completions are maximal-ideal-adic [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and the two-variable power series ring is [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Equivalently, putting $A=\mathcal O_{S,s}$, $M_h=\operatorname{Spec}(\widehat A[u,v]/(uv-h))$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $o\in M_h$ equal to the point with ideal $(\mathfrak m_A\widehat A,u,v)$, one has an isomorphism $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{T,t}\cong\widehat{\mathcal O}_{M_h,o}$ of $\widehat A$-algebras. The residue field of $o$ is $A/\mathfrak m_A$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family; split-node hypothesis spelled out using lemma-split-node. The equivalent completed-model formulation is the third paragraph of the first proof of Tag 0CBY (lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family).

proof.text: Put $A_0=\mathcal O_{S,s}$ and $B_0=\mathcal O_{T,t}$. The local map $A_0\to B_0$ is flat by the definition of flatness at $t$. To check Noetherianity of $B_0$ without assuming $S$ locally Noetherian, choose affine neighbourhoods $\operatorname{Spec}R_0$ of $s$ and $\operatorname{Spec}D$ of $t$ with $D$ finite type over $R_0$. The affine-stalk localization identifications give $A_0=(R_0)_{\mathfrak p}$ and $B_0=D_{\mathfrak q}$, with $\mathfrak q\cap R_0=\mathfrak p$. Inverting $R_0\setminus\mathfrak p$ first does not change $D_{\mathfrak q}$: each such denominator is already a unit there. Thus $B_0$ is a localization of the finite type $A_0$-algebra $D\otimes_{R_0}A_0$. This algebra, and then its localization $B_0$, are Noetherian by the two cited permanence statements.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, lemma-formal-local-structure-nodal-family, first paragraph; Tag 00FN, algebra-lemma-Noetherian-permanence; Tag 01HV, schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves

proof.text: Set $A=\widehat {A_0}$, $B=\widehat {B_0}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_{A_0}A$, and $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_{B_0}B$. The completion-local-ring statement identifies these as the maximal ideals and identifies both residue fields with $k=\kappa(s)=\kappa(t)$. The completion-Noetherian statement makes $A,B$ Noetherian. Their maximal ideals are finitely generated, and the adic-completion-mod-ideal statement makes them complete for these maximal ideals. The flat-completion statement applies to the flat local map of Noetherian local rings $A_0\to B_0$, so $A\to B$ is flat.

The fibre-stalk quotient statement gives $B_0/\mathfrak m_{A_0}B_0\cong\mathcal O_{T_s,t}$. Apply the local-completion-quotient statement to this surjection, whose source $B_0$ is Noetherian local. Its completed kernel is $\mathfrak m_{A_0}B=\mathfrak mB$, and the quotient has the induced local maximal ideal. Hence the assumed split-fibre isomorphism supplies a $k$-algebra isomorphism $B/\mathfrak mB\cong k[[x,y]]/(xy)$. Denote by $\bar u,\bar v$ the classes of $x,y$ in $B/\mathfrak mB$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, first paragraph; Tag 0CBW, curves-lemma-split-node; local completion of a quotient via Tags 00MA (algebra-lemma-completion-tensor), 00MB (algebra-lemma-completion-flat)

proof.text: Choose lifts $u_1,v_1\in B$ of $\bar u,\bar v$ and put $h_1=0$. They lie in $\mathfrak n$, and $u_1v_1-h_1\in\mathfrak mB$. More generally, every $b\in B$ can be written $b=a+u_1p+v_1q+\epsilon$ with $a\in A$, $p,q\in B$, $\epsilon\in\mathfrak mB$: reduce $b$ in $k[[x,y]]/(xy)$, subtract its constant coefficient (lifted from $k$ to $A$), and factor the remaining series into $x$ times a series plus $y$ times a series. Lift these two series classes to $B$. The same decomposition works with any $u,v$ lifting $\bar u,\bar v$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, first and second paragraphs: lifts and the decomposition of each coefficient b_i

proof.text:
For the induction step suppose $n\ge1$, $h\in\mathfrak m$, and $uv-h=\delta\in\mathfrak m^nB$, with $u,v$ lifting $\bar u,\bar v$. Write a finite sum $\delta=\sum_i f_ib_i$, $f_i\in\mathfrak m^n$, and use the preceding decomposition to write $b_i=a_i+up_i+vq_i+\epsilon_i$ with $a_i\in A$, $\epsilon_i\in\mathfrak mB$. Define $u'=u-\sum_i f_iq_i$, $v'=v-\sum_i f_ip_i$, and $h'=h+\sum_i f_ia_i$. Direct multiplication gives
$$u'v'-h'=\sum_i f_i\epsilon_i+(\sum_i f_iq_i)(\sum_j f_jp_j)\in\mathfrak m^{n+1}B,$$
since $2n\ge n+1$. Also $u'-u,v'-v\in\mathfrak m^nB$, $h'-h\in\mathfrak m^n$, and $h'\in\mathfrak m$. This proves the inductive improvement and preserves the chosen reductions.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, second paragraph, the displayed coordinate corrections and their product

proof.text: Starting from $(u_1,v_1,h_1)$, repeat the preceding improvement to obtain $u_n,v_n\in B$, $h_n\in\mathfrak m$ with consecutive differences in $\mathfrak m^nB,\mathfrak m^nB,\mathfrak m^n$ respectively and $u_nv_n-h_n\in\mathfrak m^nB$. Because $\mathfrak mB\subseteq\mathfrak n$, their reductions modulo any fixed power of $\mathfrak n$ (and of $\mathfrak m$ for $h_n$) eventually stabilize. Completeness, in the inverse-limit definition, supplies $u_\infty,v_\infty\in B$, $h\in A$ with those stabilized coordinates. The identities $u_nv_n-h_n\in\mathfrak n^n$ imply $u_\infty v_\infty=h$ by separatedness. The classes $u_\infty,v_\infty$ still lift $\bar u,\bar v$: the ideal $\mathfrak mB$ is closed for the $\mathfrak n$-adic topology, since $B/\mathfrak mB$ is a complete local quotient and hence separated for its induced maximal ideal. Likewise $\mathfrak m$ is closed in $A$, so $h\in\mathfrak m$. Only maximal-ideal completeness of $B$ is needed; no assertion of $\mathfrak mB$-adic completeness is made here.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, third paragraph, the induction and passage to limits; Tag 0325, algebra-lemma-quotient-complete-local

proof.text: Let $R=A[[x,y]]$ and $\mathfrak a=\mathfrak mR+(x,y)$. The power-series Noetherian and local-ring statements show that $R$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak a$: a series with zero constant term is $xF+yG$, so the constant-term description of that maximal ideal is exactly this sum. The complete-over-complete-base statement makes $R$ $\mathfrak a$-adically complete. Put $C=R/(xy-h)$. Since $h\in\mathfrak m$, the equation belongs to $\mathfrak a$; the complete-local-quotient statement shows that $C$ is Noetherian local and complete, with maximal ideal the image $\mathfrak a_C$ of $\mathfrak a$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, third paragraph, construction of the source algebra; Tags 0306 (algebra-lemma-Noetherian-power-series), 032C (algebra-remark-Noetherian-complete-local-ring-universally-catenary), 0325 (algebra-lemma-quotient-complete-local)

proof.text: Apply the adic-evaluation statement with coefficient map $A\to B$, ideal $\mathfrak n$, and the elements $u_\infty,v_\infty\in\mathfrak n$. It supplies an $A$-algebra homomorphism $R\to B$ sending $x,y$ to these elements. The identity $u_\infty v_\infty=h$ makes it factor through an $A$-algebra homomorphism $\phi:C\to B$. It is local: each generator of $\mathfrak a_C$, namely an element of $\mathfrak m$ or one of $x,y$, maps into $\mathfrak n$.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, third paragraph, the displayed homomorphism; universal property as used in Tag 07NL, more-algebra-lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs

proof.text: The coefficient-reduction kernel statement applies to the finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$ and gives kernel $\mathfrak mR$ for $R\to k[[x,y]]$. This map is surjective: choose in $A$ a lift of each coefficient of a given series. Since $h\in\mathfrak m$, it identifies $C/\mathfrak mC$ with $k[[x,y]]/(xy)$. The reduction of $\phi$ sends $x,y$ to $\bar u,\bar v$ and agrees with the chosen isomorphism of step 3. Indeed, modulo the $N$-th power of the maximal ideal of $B/\mathfrak mB$ both maps send a series to the image of its truncation below total degree $N$: for the reduction of $\phi$ by the explicit formula of the adic-evaluation statement, and for the chosen isomorphism because it is a $k$-algebra isomorphism of local rings, hence maps $(x,y)^N$ into the $N$-th power of the maximal ideal. Both send $x,y$ to $\bar u,\bar v$ and constants to constants, so the two maps agree at every finite truncation and then agree by separatedness of the complete local quotient $B/\mathfrak mB$. Thus $\bar\phi:C/\mathfrak mC\to B/\mathfrak mB$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, last paragraph: isomorphism after dividing by the base maximal ideal; coefficient reduction used in Tag 0EYB, pione-lemma-purity-smooth-over-depth2

proof.text: Apply the flat-mod-injective statement with its $R=A$, $S=C$, $N=C$, $M=B$, and $u=\phi$. The map $A\to C$ is local, $C$ is Noetherian, $C$ is a finite module over itself, and $B$ is flat over $A$ by step 2. Step 9 supplies the required injectivity modulo $\mathfrak m$. The statement therefore implies that $\phi$ is injective. In particular this use needs no separate flatness assertion for the hypersurface $C$.

In the closed fibre $B/\mathfrak mB\cong k[[x,y]]/(xy)$ the maximal ideal is $(\bar u,\bar v)$, by the local-ring and quotient-local-structure statements. Taking its inverse image in $B$ gives $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak mB+(u_\infty,v_\infty)B=\mathfrak a_CB$. Consequently $B/\mathfrak a_CB=k$, a one-dimensional vector space over $C/\mathfrak a_C=k$. Apply the finite-after-completion statement to the local map $C\to B$. Both maximal ideals are finitely generated since these rings are Noetherian. Because both rings are already complete for their maximal ideals, its finite completed-module conclusion identifies $B$ as a finite $C$-module via $\phi$; the completed action agrees with $\phi$ on elements by its coordinatewise definition.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, last paragraph, surjectivity by completeness; Tag 0394, algebra-lemma-finite-after-completion, applied with source C and target B

proof.text: The element $1\in B$ generates $B/\mathfrak a_CB=k$. Nakayama's local-generators statement for the finite $C$-module $B$ now implies that $1$ generates $B$ over $C$. Thus $\phi$ is surjective. Together with step 10 this gives the required $A$-algebra isomorphism $B\cong A[[x,y]]/(xy-h)$. This implements the source's completeness/surjectivity argument through the existing finite-after-completion and Nakayama interfaces.

source.place: Tag 0CBX, final paragraph; Tag 00DV, algebra-lemma-NAK, and Tag 0394, algebra-lemma-finite-after-completion

proof.text: For the equivalent polynomial-model formulation put $P=A[x,y]$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak mP+(x,y)$ and $D=P_{\mathfrak q}$. Here $P/\mathfrak q=k$, so $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. The map $P\to R=A[[x,y]]$ identifies $P/\mathfrak q^r$ with $R/\mathfrak a^r$ for every $r\ge1$: truncate above total degree $r-1$, and use the combined-ideal coefficient criterion to check that the kernel on polynomials consists exactly of those whose coefficient of $x^iy^j$ lies in $\mathfrak m^{r-i-j}$ whenever $i+j<r$. Such polynomials belong to $\mathfrak q^r$ term by term. Every denominator outside $\mathfrak q$ is already a unit in this quotient: it has an invertible constant coefficient in $A$, and its remaining part is nilpotent modulo $\mathfrak q^r$, so a finite geometric sum gives its inverse. Therefore $D/(\mathfrak qD)^r\cong R/\mathfrak a^r$, compatibly with the transition maps, constants and variables. Taking compatible sequences and using the completeness of $R$ gives $\widehat D\cong R$ as $A$-algebras.

source.place: Tag 0CBY, curves-lemma-etale-local-structure-nodal-family, first proof, third paragraph, the completed-model identification; coefficient calculation for Tag 032C

proof.text: Let $M_h=\operatorname{Spec}(P/(xy-h))$ and let $o$ be its point with ideal $\mathfrak q/(xy-h)$. Its residue field is $k$ since evaluation $x=y=0$ gives $P/(xy-h,\mathfrak m,x,y)=k$. The affine-stalk localization statement identifies $\mathcal O_{M_h,o}$ with $(P/(xy-h))_{\mathfrak q/(xy-h)}$. The fraction map identifies this ring with $D/(xy-h)D$: the denominators on both sides are exactly the images of $P\setminus\mathfrak q$, and $a/s$ is in the kernel precisely when some denominator outside $\mathfrak q$ times $a$ belongs to $(xy-h)$. The ring $D$ is Noetherian by finite-type and localization permanence over the Noetherian ring $A$. Apply local-completion-quotient to $D\to D/(xy-h)D$, and use the constant-and-variable preserving identification of step 13. It gives $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{M_h,o}\cong\widehat D/(xy-h)\widehat D\cong A[[x,y]]/(xy-h)$. Composing with step 12 proves the equivalent formulation, with its specified residue field.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q61-027d29561 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the full item and its 14 steps against curves.tex Tag 0CBX (statement and full proof), definition-split-node and lemma-split-node (0CBW), and the third paragraph of the first proof of 0CBY (the Y_sigma completed-model clause). The statement is byte-identical to the side DAG copy. Its spelled-out split-node hypothesis (closed point, kappa(t)=kappa(s), completed fibre ring isomorphic to k[[u,v]]/(uv)) drops the source's 1-dimensional fibre assumption, so it is at least as general as the source, never weaker. The source display prints 'x -> v-bar' where 'y -> v-bar' is meant; this is a typo that the worker noted. I checked the statement of each of the 25 cited nodes against each use and every hypothesis in force. Flat-completion and complete-local-quotient get Noetherian complete local inputs. Flat-mod-injective is applied with R=A, S=N=C and M=B, which is A-flat. Finite-after-completion gets finitely generated maximal ideals and B/a_C B=k. I recomputed the induction step (u'v'-h' = sum f_i eps_i + product, which lies in m^{n+1}B because n>=1). The lifts survive the limit because mB is closed: B/mB is a separated complete local quotient. Step 13's polynomial-to-power-series comparison holds through the combined-ideal criterion plus the fact that denominators become units mod q^r. Edge cases checked: A0=k, the family xy=t over k[[t]], characteristic 2, h zero or nilpotent, S not locally Noetherian, mixed characteristic. There are no new nodes and no duplicates: only the two citers mention 0CBX or uv-h. All 10 declared tool_uses are accepted as generic commutative-algebra black boxes, and they are exactly the split, non-closed off-unit dependencies. No SGA source is used, and this is not a target node.
